messages:
sre-oncall: seeing a spike of 504/502 from apiserver in eu-central1 since ~16:02 UTC, manifests as failed controller-manager leader renewals and stalled GPU pod provisioning :rotating_light:
maya: on it — looking at apiserver logs and kube-proxy metrics now
sam: grabbing `kubectl -n kube-system logs kube-apiserver-0` and `kubectl get endpoints --all-namespaces`
sam: logs show repeated `etcdserver: request timed out` and `proxy read timeout` interleaved with `connection reset by peer`
maya: also seeing a lot of `TCP_RETRANSMIT` on the NAT gateway for the kube-proxy node pool (nat-gw-euc-1)
olivia: are we seeing packet drops or just idle timeouts? I can run pings/traceroute from a few nodes to the etcd hosts
liam: GCP pushed a proxy update last night in eu-central that changed backend idle timeout to 90s — could explain the TTLs on long-lived connections to etcd
maya: suggested mitigation: lower kube-proxy conntrack `tcp-timeout` and bump keepalive on apiserver -> etcd client to 30s, then roll kube-proxy DaemonSet to the node pool
sam: applied kube-proxy config to 3/5 nodes as a canary:
```
# kubectl -n kube-system patch ds kube-proxy --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-proxy","env":[{"name":"GODEBUG","value":"tcpkeepalive=30"}]}]}}}}'
```
maya: applied! monitoring grafana dashboard `controlplane.network` — 504s dropped by ~70% on the patched nodes
olivia: confirming reduced retransmits from patched nodes, NAT gateway counters still elevated though
liam: long-term: we need persistent keepalive config in our apiserver flags and consider migrating etcd endpoints behind an internal load balancer with health checks to avoid proxy idle kills
maya: created a runbook snippet in confluence and opened a DR ticket: incident/1765004321 — includes rollback steps for the kube-proxy patch and verification queries (eg `kubectl get endpoints`, `kubectl top pods -n kube-system`)
sre-oncall: nice work, teams — can we schedule a follow-up to decide LB vs keepalive change? also need to quantify cost impact of LB in eu-central vs moving some GPU provisioning to w-europe (cost + latency tradeoffs)
liam: I'll run a quick cost delta for internal LB + extra bandwidth vs cross-region provisioning — will post numbers in ~1h
sam: for immediate stability I'll finish rolling kube-proxy to remaining nodes, will keep canary window 10m between nodes
maya: FYI deploy-bot started a controller-manager canary rollout to ensure leader election stable after proxy patches
deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated: controller-manager v2.3.1 -> 3 nodes, 2m interval
sre-oncall: watching metrics; mark incident as mitigated when apiserver 5xxs < 1% for 15m
olivia: will keep an eye on NAT gateway metrics and file a support case with cloud provider if counters don't drop post-rollout
liam: cost note: internal LB in eu-central has ~+0.9c/hr per IP + small egress, moving 20% of GPU fleet to w-europe would add ~12ms median latency but saves ~18% on persistent infra cost — will share exact numbers
maya: thanks — adding postmortem owners and assigning action items in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
